title: Evidence for a male-biased sex ratio in the offspring of a large herbivore: The role of environmental conditions in the sex ratio variation

claims.text: Number of tagged roe deer fawns with known sex in Baden-Württemberg, 1972–2019
claims.statistic: sample size (count of fawns with sex recorded)
claims.location: Abstract; Methods 2.1 ('For 3280 of 12,437 marked fawns'); Table 1 caption; Figure 1 caption. Conflicts with Table 2 row ref 47 and Table 3 row ID 90 (12473, '12,473') and with Metafor_roe_sex.csv Hagen row (N = 12475)
claims.notes: Rows with Sex in {f,m} and Year 1972-2019 (stated exclusions only). Hasl-NA rows kept; N excluding Hasl-NA = 11793. Raw file rows = 17260.

claims.text: Proportion of female offspring among tagged fawns in Baden-Württemberg is below parity (male-biased), 95% CI from exact binomial test
claims.statistic: proportion female with exact (Clopper-Pearson) binomial 95% CI
claims.location: Table 2, row reference 47 'Hagen et al., this publication'; also Table 3 row ID 90
claims.notes: pf = 5941/12435; exact Clopper-Pearson 95% CI [0.4690, 0.4866] (binom.test); p vs 0.5. Without Hasl-NA rows: pf = 0.4793 [0.4702, 0.4883], n = 11793.

claims.text: Overall effect size d for the prenatal sex ratio (random-effects model, data-set level) is negative, i.e. male-biased
claims.statistic: random-effects meta-analytic mean of d = ln(OR)/(pi/sqrt(3)), OR = pf/(1-pf)
claims.location: Results 3.2, paragraph after Table 3 (and Figure 3 / Appendix Figure S1)
claims.notes: metafor rma REML on 37 prenatal rows (paper says 36); tau2 = 0.00137, I2 = 13.59%.

claims.text: Overall effect size d for the secondary sex ratio (random-effects model, data-set level) is negative, i.e. male-biased
claims.location: Results 3.2, paragraph after Table 3 (and Figure 3). The fixed model at reference level gives the identical −0.04 [−0.06, −0.03]
claims.notes: metafor rma REML on 15 secondary rows; tau2 = 0.00000, I2 = 0.01%.

claims.text: Mean temperature Oct(t−1)–Feb(t) (linear term) is associated with offspring sex in the binomial GLM (Equation 2)
claims.statistic: binomial GLM coefficient (logit), sex 1=female ~ f(T Oct–Feb) + f(P Sep), f(x)=a0+a1x+a2x^2
claims.notes: glm binomial logit, n = 11793 (Hasl-NA dropped); T_cor = mean(Oct-Dec t-1, Jan-Feb t) - 0.65*Hasl/100; P_Sep raw mm. Uncorrected-T sensitivity: -0.0041 (SE 0.0904, p 0.964).

claims.text: Quadratic term of mean temperature Oct(t−1)–Feb(t) is positive and significant: relatively cold or warm autumn/winters deviate from the male-biased mean (U-shaped)
claims.notes: Quadratic T_cor term, same model as C5. Uncorrected-T sensitivity: -0.00113 (SE 0.01472, p 0.939).
